chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The first one to variegate [goods] was Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and the first one to soften Al-Tharid was Hashim.'

key_terms.الثَّرِيدَ: Tharid, a traditional dish of bread soaked in meat broth
key_terms.لَوَّنَ: to vary, to display with variety, or to color/mix
key_terms.هَاشِمٌ: Hashim, grandfather of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW)
key_terms.هَشَمَ: to soften, to crush, or to break (referring to the bread in Tharid)

ai.seo_question: Who was the first person to variegate goods and soften Tharid according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the noble lineage of Hashim ibn Abd Manaf, emphasizing his role in pioneering the preparation of Tharid, a dish of bread soaked in broth, which became a symbol of hospitality and generosity in pre-Islamic and early Islamic Arabia. By linking this culinary distinction to the Prophet’s family, the narration underscores the spiritual and social virtues of generosity and service that characterize the Ahl al-Bayt, reinforcing their status as exemplars of ethical conduct in daily life.
